method: Each of six full source images directly inspected separately against its production prompt. No contact-sheet-only review.
scope: Finished individual gallery key art; not rigs or gameplay verification.

evidence: The shield forearm visibly operates the furnace door while the opposite sword controls the approach lane.
Adult face, worn materials and planted feet hold the physical-realism bar.
The circular excavation, elevator and cold/ember light match the furnace region.
nonblocking_limits: Shield forearm reads as a compact forged gauntlet rather than a broad shield; enough functional identity survives for the still.

evidence: Ventral feeding mouth, translucent fin ribbons and displaced fish make the organism distinct from a generic dragon.
Broad curved body across the portrait frame communicates scale and movement.
Underwater architecture, divers and veiling water match the Pelagic Cathedral.
nonblocking_limits: Fin roots overlap and extend beyond frame, so exact four-pair construction is not proven by this view; visible anatomy remains plausible.

evidence: Pitted bronze, soaked cloth, planted stone pavise and a precarious bridge produce an adult military threat.
Underwater region and relative scale are coherent.
publication_blockers: The held weapon forks into two long crossing shafts at the grip: the hand holds a near-horizontal staff while a separate diagonal standard rises through it. The connection is not visually established as an intentional mechanism. Replace with one continuous shaft from grip to hooked head, with a short visible butt behind the hand.
nonblocking_limits: A planted stance reads better than a sweeping action; a clear single hooked shaft will suffice for key-art publication.

evidence: External resonator struts, featherless bird anatomy and the bill inside a huge ceramic bell give strong owned identity.
Concentric dust establishes the acoustic action without arbitrary light effects.
Wine textiles, ceramic bell chambers and tiny human scale are consistent with the burial-bell region.
nonblocking_limits: Some rib roots are occluded; this is a persuasive creature still rather than a complete anatomical diagram.

evidence: Distinct older human antagonist with readable ceramic ear guards, cracked resonator and hammer contact.
Challenger foreground and rising dust connect the visual to an imminent encounter.
Burial-bell materials and spatial repetition pair coherently with b05.
nonblocking_limits: Vaust looks toward the challenger beside rather than through the resonator; this minor staging deviation is not a publication blocker.

evidence: Climbing posture, loaded wall contact and joint membranes make the arthropod physically persuasive.
Raised blade limbs and armoured segmented mass provide a distinctive canopy-predator silhouette.
Aqueduct, rust foliage, deep ravine and distant watch platform establish regional continuity.
nonblocking_limits: Rear legs overlap in the lower body silhouette; exact limb-root topology cannot be established from this oblique still. Avoid labelling it an anatomy turnaround.

conclusion: Five accepted. b04 requires one focused weapon-grip continuity repair before publication. No childish styling observed in this batch.
